entries.name: Sarang Kitchen
entries.description: A Korean fried chicken restaurant in Toronto opened by a chef and a special education teacher who set out to hire neurodivergent staff and welcome neurodivergent guests. It keeps sensory-friendly hours before 9pm with calming music and reduced lighting, lends sensory boxes with fidgets, weighted blankets and noise-cancelling headphones, and has a multi-sensory room for guests who feel overstimulated or anxious.
entries.cost_note: Restaurant menu prices; tipping discouraged (Hospitality Included pricing)
entries.evidence: Our sensory boxes and multi-sensory room allow guests to dine in our restaurant at ease knowing that there are fidgets, weighted blankets, and noise-cancelling headphones they can use
entries.notes: Its own site (footer on every page, checked 2026-10-20) lists two Toronto locations, 1056 Bloor St W and 774 Danforth Ave, and its Media page lists a CityNews story titled 'Danforth Restaurant Goes to the Dogs with Special K9 Menu', so listing 55a5f60e ('Danforth Avenue') looks like the real second branch, not a duplicate of the Bloor listing; df308601 (checked list, no address) is the same business as this one. Its catering page instead prints 703 Danforth Ave and 2450 Bloor St W with two phone numbers, which conflicts with the footer, so phone is left null and addresses should be confirmed. A Holland Bloorview BLOOM article (May 2023) says it opened at 1056 Bloor St. W in March 2023 and that four of nine staff had disabilities like autism or ADHD.

entries.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
entries.description: The aquarium in downtown Toronto runs Sensory Sunday Mornings, developed with Autism Ontario, with increased lighting, no music and a quiet room for guests who need a break. It is a Certified Autism Center (IBCCES): staff have autism awareness training and sensory guides are posted at each exhibit.
entries.cost_note: Sensory Sunday Mornings are included with general admission
entries.evidence: On Sensory Sunday Mornings, there is increased lighting, a music-free environment, and a quiet room for guests who require a break.
entries.notes: Upcoming dates on its page when checked: Nov 8 and Dec 6, 2026. A Destination Toronto article (updated May 2025) says Sensory Sundays are on the first Sunday of every month and that it was the first Canadian attraction to become a Certified Autism Center.

entries.name: Toronto Zoo
entries.description: Toronto's large zoo publishes a sensory map of Headphone Zones and Quiet Areas and lends KultureCity sensory bags (noise-reducing headphones, sunglasses, fidget toys, visual cue cards) from its Accessibility Hub. It also has its own MagnusCards visual step-by-step guides for autistic and neurodiverse visitors.
entries.cost_note: Zoo admission; sensory bags are signed out and returned at the Accessibility Hub
entries.evidence: This map identifies Headphone Zones and Quiet Areas to help our guests prepare for a visit.
entries.notes: A zoo events page for sensory-friendly early admission on weekends and holidays (found in search) now returns HTTP 410, so that early-admission program could not be confirmed for 2026; the sensory map, sensory bags and MagnusCards are on the current accessibility page.

entries.name: Royal Ontario Museum (ROM)
entries.description: Toronto's museum of natural history and world cultures publishes a Sensory Friendly Guide for visitors that warns which galleries get loud or crowded, suggests the quietest times to come, and points to a quiet area on the 3rd floor.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission; attendants supporting a person with a disability get in free
entries.evidence: If you want to visit the museum when it is quiet, we suggest that you visit after 2 pm on a weekday during the school year.
entries.notes: Destination Toronto (updated May 2025) adds that visitors can ask any security guard for the First Aid and Special Needs Room if they need more privacy.

entries.name: Low Sensory Mornings (CN Tower)
entries.description: On scheduled Sundays the CN Tower runs Low Sensory Mornings for 90 minutes after opening, made with Autism Ontario and Variety Village: fewer people in the elevators, adjusted lighting and audio-visual elements, no music, a quiet space, social stories and free sensory kits. Staff are trained through Autism Ontario.
entries.cost_note: Regular tickets; sensory kits are free to borrow with ID
entries.evidence: In partnership with Autism Ontario and Variety Village, we have adapted the CN Tower experience to provide our guests with sensory sensitivities further ways to enjoy their visit.
entries.notes: Dates listed when checked: Sunday October 4, October 18, November 1 and November 29 (2026). The page notes that The Top level's small elevator and viewing areas may be hard for people with sensory sensitivities.

entries.name: Rogers Centre (Toronto Blue Jays)
entries.description: The Toronto Blue Jays' stadium, also used for concerts, is certified Sensory Inclusive by KultureCity. Sensory bags with noise-cancelling headphones, fidget tools, cue cards and weighted lap pads are available at any Fan Services booth, and there are quiet areas, a sensory room at Section 212 and a social story to plan a visit.
entries.cost_note: Game or concert ticket; sensory bags are free at Fan Services
entries.evidence: Rogers Centre is proud to be a Sensory Inclusive Certified venue by KultureCity.
entries.notes: Its Sensory Room page says the room (Section 212, behind Fan Services) is open at all Rogers Centre events and suits fans with autism and other sensory processing needs. Destination Toronto (updated May 2025) describes bean bags, weighted lap pads and a bubble wall.

entries.name: Canadian Museum of Nature
entries.description: The natural history museum in Ottawa lends sensory bags for free at its membership desk, filled with items that help visitors with sensory needs have a more comfortable visit, and lets one person accompanying a visitor with a disability in for free.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission; sensory bags free to borrow; one accompanying person free
entries.evidence: Borrow a sensory bag for free during your visit to the museum.
entries.notes: Its 'find out more about sensory bags' link goes to the Ottawa Museum Network's sensory bag program page, which describes what the bags contain; bags are first-come, first-served.

entries.name: Canada Science and Technology Museum (Ingenium)
entries.description: Ottawa's science and technology museum lends sensory kits (noise-cancelling headphones, sunglasses, fidget toys) at the front desk and offers downloadable sensory guides designed to support autistic visitors; exhibitions with sound have volume controls and headphone jacks.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission; sensory kits on request at the front desk
entries.evidence: You can borrow a sensory kit, which includes noise-cancelling headphones, sunglasses, fidget toys, and more.
entries.notes: Search results mention low-sensory 'Mellow Mornings' here, but that event page now returns 404, so only the sensory kits and guides are confirmed.

entries.name: Sensory Bag Program (Ottawa Museum Network)
entries.description: Free sensory bags at all twelve community museums in the Ottawa Museum Network, including the Bytown Museum, the Diefenbunker and Cumberland Heritage Village. Each bag has ear defenders, sunglasses, fidget toys, colour communication cards and a museum activity, and there is an access guide to prepare visitors with sensory sensitivities.
entries.cost_note: Bags are free to borrow during a museum visit (museum admission may apply)
entries.evidence: Sensory bags are now available at all museums in our network. Each bag is filled with resources to help visitors with various sensory needs have a more enjoyable museum experience.
entries.notes: Booking differs by museum (walk-up, online form, or phone 48 hours ahead for City of Ottawa museums); the page lists each museum's phone number. Funded in part by the federal Enabling Accessibility Fund.

entries.name: Sensory Sundays (Bank of Canada Museum)
entries.description: On select Sundays the Bank of Canada Museum in Ottawa opens early (9 to 10 am) for a sensory-friendly visit with reduced sound, extra signs, a quiet area, hands-on artifacts and crafts, and noise-cancelling headphones, fidget toys and sunglasses to borrow; a social story helps prepare.
entries.cost_note: Not stated on the Sensory Sundays page
entries.evidence: We’re turning down the lights and the volume for our sensory-sensitive visitors—explore the Museum using more than eyes and ears.
entries.notes: When checked the site also showed a banner saying 'The Museum is temporarily closed', while the Sensory Sundays page lists November 29, 2026; confirm the museum has reopened before publishing.

entries.name: Lil E Coffee Cafe (Toronto)
entries.description: A non-profit coffee shop at Yonge and St. Clair in Toronto staffed by young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Staff work through an 18-to-24-month training program, with visual drink guides, break timers and emotion check-ins, and are then helped into longer-term jobs with partner employers.
entries.cost_note: Café prices
entries.evidence: We’re a coffee shop with two locations and one very big dream to empower people with intellectual and developmental disabilities with life skills they need to thrive in the workplace and beyond.
entries.notes: Open Monday to Friday 8:00am to 4:00pm per its site (checked 2026-10-20). The phone number on its site is the organisation's Calgary number. Training-program details (length, supports) are from a Streets of Toronto article written soon after the Toronto café opened (2023).

entries.name: The Coffee Shed (Common Ground Co-operative)
entries.description: Two Toronto coffee shops (at Surrey Place and at the University of Toronto's New College) run as businesses by adults with developmental disabilities, including autistic adults, who are Partners in the business, with support from Common Ground Co-operative. They sell coffee, baked goods, salads and sandwiches.
entries.cost_note: Café prices
entries.evidence: The Coffee Sheds are social enterprises proudly operated by adults with developmental disabilities.
entries.notes: Locations: 2 Surrey Place (phone (416) 925-2169 ext. 2403) and New College, 300 Huron Street (phone used here); a third location is 'coming soon'. Common Ground Co-operative has supported Toronto adults with autism, Down syndrome and other developmental disabilities in social enterprises since 2000.

entries.name: The Owl Cafe (Y's Owl Maclure)
entries.description: A café and meeting place in Ottawa run as a social enterprise by Y's Owl Maclure Co-operative Centre, which supports people with autism and developmental disabilities. It gives autistic people and people with disabilities paid work, skills and confidence in a supportive setting, and is open to the public on weekdays.
entries.cost_note: Café prices
entries.evidence: It creates meaningful employment opportunities for people with disabilities and Autistic people within a welcoming and supportive environment.
entries.notes: Cafe hours on its page: Monday to Friday from 9:00 am, to 8:00 pm on Tuesdays and Fridays; closed weekends. The address is Y's Owl Maclure's (Suite 100); the existing listing places the café at the same address.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (Young People's Theatre)
entries.description: Toronto's theatre for young audiences runs Relaxed Performances with a relaxed attitude to theatre rules, slightly adjusted sound and lighting, a calm area for breaks and resources before and during the show. 'Meet the Theatre' visits let nervous or first-time theatre-goers see the space beforehand.
entries.cost_note: Theatre tickets; support persons free; pay-what-you-wish performances offered
entries.evidence: Relaxed Performances include extra features to make the theatre-going experience more sensory-friendly, including a relaxed attitude to our general rules, slightly adjusted sound and lighting levels, a calm area if a break is needed
entries.notes: 2026-27 season lists a schools relaxed performance on Monday, October 19 and a public one on Sunday, March 7 (printed as 2026, probably 2027). A TDSB autism services co-ordinator is quoted praising the accommodations for audience members with ASD.

entries.name: Sensory Sundays (Science North)
entries.description: Sudbury's science centre holds Sensory Sundays with sounds turned down or off, adjusted lighting, fewer visitors, sensory break spaces and a sensory-friendly IMAX film with house lights on and lower volume. On any day, Sensory Backpacks with noise-cancelling earmuffs, fidget toys, sunglasses and timers can be borrowed at Science North and Dynamic Earth.
entries.cost_note: Science centre admission; Sensory Backpacks lent free on request
entries.evidence: During this event, sounds will be turned down or off, lighting will be adjusted, the science centre will be less busy, and certain spaces will be set up as sensory break spaces.
entries.notes: The pages checked do not list 2026-27 Sensory Sunday dates. Autism Ontario has also run a Sensory Friendly Sunday here for its member families (event page undated).

entries.name: Sensory Friendly Evenings (London Children's Museum)
entries.description: Free monthly evenings at London's children's museum for children with autism, disabilities or sensory processing needs and their families, with very limited attendance, less noise and fewer crowds. On regular days the museum has a quiet room, Adventure Backpacks with noise-cancelling headphones, timers, a social story and visual supports, and weighted lap blankets to borrow.
entries.cost_note: Sensory Friendly Evenings are free; register in advance
entries.evidence: Sensory Friendly Evenings offer children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), physical or cognitive disabilities, or sensory processing considerations, and their families with a quieter museum experience.
entries.notes: Dates listed when checked: October 20, November 3 (sensory-friendly trick-or-treat) and November 17, 2026, 5:00 to 8:00 pm. Funded by the Ontario Trillium Foundation and private donors.

entries.name: Museum London
entries.description: Museum London lends Autism Canada's Sensory Support Kits for free at its welcome desk, with noise-reducing ear covers, fidget items and tinted glasses to help with visual sensitivity.
entries.cost_note: Sensory kits are free to borrow with ID
entries.evidence: We provide free kits which include noise reducing ear covers, fidget items (cube, spinner, squishy ball) and tinted safety glasses to help manage visual sensitivity.
entries.notes: Kits are first-come, first-served. The page does not state museum admission prices, so cost refers to the kits.

entries.name: Canada Agriculture and Food Museum (Ingenium)
entries.description: A working farm and museum in Ottawa that publishes a sensory guide and a map of sensory considerations (loud barn fans, strong smells, unpredictable animals, bright crowded play areas) so visitors can plan which parts to visit or avoid, and lends sensory tools at the admission booth.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission; sensory tools lent on request
entries.evidence: Please ask at the Admission Booth if you would like to borrow sensory tools when you arrive.
entries.notes: Sensory guide PDF dated November 2025. Two existing listings for this museum (0c17741a as Museum, 7b66ade5 as Zoo & Aquarium) look like duplicates of each other; matched to the Museum one.

entries.name: Sensory-friendly swims and Snoezelen pool (City of Mississauga)
entries.description: Mississauga runs sensory-friendly public swims with reduced noise, limited capacity and calming music at Churchill Meadows and Mississauga Valleys community centres, and Snoezelen pool sessions with soft lighting, music and multisensory equipment for people with autism or sensory processing needs at Malton Community Centre and Huron Park Recreation Centre.
entries.cost_note: Fees not stated in the news story
entries.evidence: For sensory-friendly swims, participants can expect reduced noise levels, limited capacity, a quieter setting, and calming music for a relaxed atmosphere.
entries.notes: The city's current Adapted programs page still describes the Snoezelen Pool Program (dimmed lights, soft water sprays, soothing visuals; for people with disabilities, ASD, dementia or brain injuries, no diagnosis required). Sensory-friendly swim locations are from a city news story dated January 31, 2025; check the current swim schedule. Snoezelen sessions do not teach swimming.

entries.name: Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery (KWAG)
entries.description: A free public art gallery in Kitchener's Centre In The Square with a detailed sensory guide: it is fragrance-reduced, uses soft lighting, lets visitors skip the front desk, warns about the echoing lobby, and staff will take anyone who feels overwhelmed to a quiet room or low-lit space to reset. Its monthly Sensory Saturdays for autistic and neurodivergent visitors (reduced light and volume, run since 2020) are paused until a redesigned version returns.
entries.cost_note: Admission is free for everyone; support persons free
entries.address: 101 Queen Street North, Kitchener, ON N2H 6P7
entries.evidence: If you feel overwhelmed, overstimulated, or anxious at any point, please let any staff member know. We will guide you to a quiet room or a low-lit administrative space where you can sit in privacy and reset.
entries.notes: Sensory Saturdays are paused while the gallery redesigns them; its access page says a new 'Access Saturday' is coming by January 2027. The 2020 launch post describes reduced lobby lighting and lower volume on video artworks.

entries.name: Sensory Friendly Screenings (The Westdale)
entries.description: An independent cinema in Hamilton that runs Sensory Friendly Screenings with theatre lights dimmed rather than dark, lower sound, open captions, no ads or trailers, a quiet room, and freedom to move around the theatre.
entries.cost_note: Regular cinema ticket prices
entries.evidence: They include Open Captioning during the film, dimmed theatre lights instead of dark, a lower sound level, no advertisements or trailers, a quiet room, and audience members can feel free to roam the theatre.
entries.notes: Sensory-friendly showtimes are marked in its listings of accessible films; no fixed schedule is given. Active Parents' Halton-Hamilton sensory-friendly guide also lists these screenings.

entries.name: TD Place (Lansdowne)
entries.description: Ottawa's arena and stadium at Lansdowne (home of the REDBLACKS and 67's) lends free sensory kits with sunglasses, noise-reducing earmuffs and fidget toys, has a quiet room near section 1 for sensory regulation, can set aside quiet areas on request, and publishes picture sensory guides for REDBLACKS and 67's games.
entries.cost_note: Event tickets; sensory kits free with ID held until return
entries.evidence: TD Place offers kits with tools that reduce the stimulus often associated with sporting and entertainment events.
entries.notes: Kits are signed out at Guest Experience booths (Section 18 in the arena, Section S in the stadium). Ask Guest Experience at least one business day ahead to arrange a quiet area; it varies by event.

entries.name: Meridian Centre
entries.description: The arena and event centre in downtown St. Catharines is certified Sensory Inclusive by KultureCity: staff are trained to help guests with sensory needs, and sensory bags with noise-cancelling headphones, fidget tools and emotion cards can be borrowed at the Box Office during any event. A video walkthrough shows what an event is like beforehand.
entries.cost_note: Event tickets; sensory bags borrowed at the Box Office
entries.evidence: The Meridian Centre is proud to be Kulture City Sensory Inclusive Certified. This certification ensures our staff are trained and prepared to assist guests with sensory needs
entries.notes: Box Office in-person hours are weekdays 12pm to 5pm. Address from its Directions & Parking page.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (Shaw Festival)
entries.description: The Shaw Festival theatre in Niagara-on-the-Lake stages Relaxed Performances for people with sensory sensitivities, autism, learning differences or anxiety: no one expects silence or stillness, and audience members can move, vocalize, react naturally or take a break, with a relaxed performance booklet to prepare.
entries.cost_note: Theatre tickets
entries.evidence: These performances are especially helpful for individuals who may benefit from a more casual environment; including people with sensory sensitivities, autism, dementia or Alzheimer’s, learning differences, anxiety or anyone who simply prefers a gentler theatre experience.
entries.notes: 2026 relaxed performances included The Wind in the Willows (July 8) and Rodgers + Hammerstein's Cinderella; the season has ended, so check the 2027 schedule. Guidebooks are being revised. A Niagara Now story (July 31, 2024) describes a relaxed Secret Garden run with Autism Ontario, with a quiet space and fidget items, attended by over 120 people.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (The Grand Theatre)
entries.description: London's Grand Theatre offers Relaxed Performances for neurodivergent audiences, including autistic people and people with ADHD, sensory or learning disabilities: patrons can leave and re-enter, light and sound are reduced, and startling effects like strobe lights and fog are removed. A venue guide shows the building in advance.
entries.cost_note: Theatre tickets
entries.evidence: Relaxed Performances are intended to be sensitive to and welcoming of Neurodivergent Audiences, including patrons on the autism spectrum, those with sensory and communication disorders, ADHD, learning or developmental disabilities
entries.notes: 2026/27 relaxed performance listed: A Christmas Carol, Sunday, December 13, 2026, 1:00 p.m. Young children and babes in arms are welcome at relaxed performances.

entries.name: Relaxed Screenings (Hot Docs Ted Rogers Cinema)
entries.description: Toronto's documentary cinema holds Relaxed Screenings, a sensory-friendly and more informal way to watch films for neurodivergent viewers and anyone who prefers it, alongside captioned and audio-described screenings.
entries.cost_note: Cinema tickets
entries.evidence: Relaxed Screenings: These screenings offer a sensory friendly environment for those in the neuro-diverse community or for anyone who may benefit from a more informal viewing atmosphere.
entries.notes: The accessibility page does not list dates or exactly what changes at a relaxed screening; it suggests contacting the Box Office for current accessible screenings.

entries.name: Canada's Wonderland
entries.description: Canada's largest theme park, in Vaughan, has a dedicated quiet room at the front gate for guests with sensory processing concerns, ride access passes through its Attraction Accessibility Program, and rides rated on a 'thrill' scale so families can choose what suits them.
entries.cost_note: Park admission
entries.evidence: The park provides accessibility programs and services, including ride access passes, a dedicated quiet room for guests with sensory processing concerns
entries.notes: The park's own accessibility page lists 'Quiet Room at Front Gate' and an 'Attraction Accessibility Program' but the details are in a downloadable guide; the quiet-room description is from Destination Ontario (updated August 2026).

entries.name: Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO)
entries.description: One of Canada's major art museums, in Toronto, offers a downloadable sensory map and a visual guide that explains the visit step by step to reduce anxiety, and lends sensory kits with noise-reducing headphones, fidget toys and sunglasses from its Multisensory Art Cart.
entries.cost_note: Gallery admission
entries.evidence: Download the sensory map with detailed information for navigating the gallery and the visual guide, which helps reduce anxiety by detailing the AGO experience.
entries.notes: BLOCKED: https://ago.ca/ and its accessibility and Multisensory Art Cart pages returned HTTP 403 to our fetcher; details are from Destination Ontario (updated August 28, 2026). Website set to that article; swap in https://ago.ca/events/multisensory-art-cart on review.

entries.name: Sensory Swims, Sensory Skates and sensory kits (Town of Oakville)
entries.description: Oakville runs Sensory Swims on Thursdays at Oakville Trafalgar Community Centre and Sensory Skates on Saturdays at Sixteen Mile Sports Complex, drop-ins with fewer people and a calmer, sensory-friendly space. Sensory kits with noise-cancelling headphones, fidget toys and colouring sheets can be borrowed at community centre desks.
entries.cost_note: Drop-in fees not stated on the page; sensory kits lent for use on site
entries.evidence: Sensory Skates and Sensory Swims are inclusive community drop-ins with a lower participant capacity, a more relaxing environment and sensory-friendly space.
entries.notes: Sensory kits are for ages 3+ and must be returned before closing. The same page describes inclusion support for town programs (one-on-one Aquadapt swim lessons, support persons).

entries.name: Judy's Beach Café
entries.description: A non-profit café in Toronto's Beaches neighbourhood (at Queen and Balsam) founded by two former special education teachers to train and employ people with intellectual or developmental disabilities in paid jobs. It serves coffee, baked goods and light meals and is set up as a community gathering space.
entries.cost_note: Café prices
entries.evidence: Judy’s Beach Café is more than a café — it’s a non-profit social enterprise that provides job training and employment to people with intellectual or developmental disabilities.
entries.notes: Its own website loads only with JavaScript (no readable text for our checker); details are from a Streets of Toronto article written soon after it opened (it employed 10 people with disabilities). A Global News video titled 'Beach café employs people with disabilities' is dated August 6, 2026. Autism is not named specifically in the sources.

entries.name: Dental Clinic (The Ottawa Hospital)
entries.description: A hospital dental clinic at the Civic Campus in Ottawa for adults who cannot be safely treated in a community dental office, including adults with severe developmental disabilities or complex cognitive or mental health needs. Its Dental Assist Program adds an extra assistant for patients with behaviour or anxiety needs, and it has cared for autistic adults who could not manage a regular cleaning.
entries.cost_note: Not stated; referral letter asks for insurance information
entries.evidence: Referrals are accepted for adults (18 years and older) who meet one or more of the following criteria and follow the referral process: Complex physical, cognitive or mental health challenges. Severe developmental disabilities.
entries.notes: Referral only (a doctor or dentist sends a referral letter, medication list and recent x-rays); consultations may be delayed three to four months. Dental anxiety alone does not qualify. The autism story and Dental Assist Program are from a hospital news article dated September 24, 2021; the clinic page is current.

entries.name: The Lunchbox Café & Catering (Community Living North Halton)
entries.description: A café in Milton run as a social enterprise by Community Living North Halton, where adults with developmental disabilities train in food preparation, serving and customer service. It serves homemade breakfast and lunch to the public on weekdays and also offers catering and meeting rooms.
entries.cost_note: Café and catering prices
entries.evidence: The Lunchbox Café provides adults with developmental disabilities the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the food and hospitality industry.
entries.notes: Source is Community Living North Halton's own post dated September 3, 2026. Phone and email are the agency's; the café also has its own website linked from the post. Autism is not named specifically, though the agency runs autism services.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (The National Ballet of Canada)
entries.description: The National Ballet of Canada in Toronto holds shortened, low-cost Relaxed Performances for neurodiverse and disabled audiences, with a relaxed entry and exit policy, a quiet room for breaks, a venue guide and fact sheet to prepare, extra staff, softer lobby announcements and house lights kept on low.
entries.cost_note: Offered at a nominal price
entries.evidence: Offered at a nominal price, these performances ensure that audiences who are Neurodiverse, members of the d/Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Blind/Partially Sighted and Disability Communities feel safe, welcome and cared for.
entries.notes: The page says the 2026/27 relaxed performance is 'coming soon' (no date yet). ASL interpretation and live audio description are also offered at these performances.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (Stratford Festival)
entries.description: The Stratford Festival theatre runs relaxed performances designed especially for autistic and neurodiverse people, families and first-time theatregoers: lighting and sound are adjusted, and audience members are free to move around, make noise or take breaks outside the auditorium.
entries.cost_note: Theatre tickets
entries.evidence: These performances are especially designed to support autistic and neurodiverse individuals, as well as families, young children and first-time theatregoers.
entries.notes: The 2026 relaxed performance was Something Rotten! on Friday, August 28 at 2 p.m. (Festival Theatre), per a ConnectABILITY post of June 2026; check for 2027 dates. The festival's own relaxed-performance page returned compressed data our checker could not read; a My Stratford Now story describes an earlier relaxed performance with house lights partly on.

entries.name: Sensory Support Kits (Barrie Public Library)
entries.description: Barrie's public library lends Autism Canada's Sensory Support Kits, made to support people on the autism spectrum, with noise-reducing ear covers, fidget items and tinted glasses for visual sensitivity. Kits can be borrowed for up to three weeks, placed on hold and returned to any branch.
entries.cost_note: Borrowed with a library card; no late fees, replacement fee if lost or damaged
entries.evidence: Developed by Autism Canada, Sensory Support Kits are designed to support those on the Autism Spectrum by offering a selection of sensory and tactile items for self-regulation, comfort and to stimulate learning.
entries.notes: Part of the library's Library of Things (limit two items per card). Matched to the Downtown Branch listing; kits can be picked up at any Barrie Public Library location.

entries.name: Sensory Kits (St. Catharines Public Library)
entries.description: Every St. Catharines Public Library branch lends sensory kits developed by Autism Canada for people of any age to use during a library visit, with noise-reducing headphones, tinted sunglasses, a fleece blanket, a plush toy and fidget items for self-regulation and comfort.
entries.cost_note: Checked out to a library card for up to 3 hours in the library; no fee stated
entries.evidence: Sensory kits provide a selection of sensory and tactile items for self-regulation and comfort. The kits were developed by Autism Canada and have additional items from 5 Senses of Fun.
entries.notes: Funded by a Niagara Community Foundation Mini Grant. Matched to the Central Library listing; kits are at all branches.

entries.name: Sensory Kits (Burlington Public Library)
entries.description: Six of Burlington Public Library's seven branches have a sensory kit, made with Autism Canada for neurodiverse customers of any age, with noise-cancelling headphones, sunglasses, fidget toys, a light-up wand and a lava 'hourglass' to use in the branch.
entries.cost_note: Free to use in the library (per Active Parents), checked out to a library card for up to three hours
entries.evidence: Our kits are designed to provide comfort to neuro-diverse people through self-soothing tactile items that can help reduce anxiety and stress in unfamiliar environments.
entries.notes: Library announcement dated February 27, 2023 (over two years old); Active Parents' current Halton-Hamilton guide still lists the kits at 6 of 7 branches. Kits are not available to take home. Matched to the Central Branch listing.

entries.name: Sensory Support Kits (Bradford West Gwillimbury Public Library)
entries.description: The public library in Bradford West Gwillimbury lends Autism Canada's Sensory Support Kits in a red backpack, with noise-reducing ear covers, fidget toys, tinted glasses, a fleece blanket, a plush bear and a sensory book, to help people who struggle with sensory overload stay calm on outings.
entries.cost_note: Checked out with a library card; no fee stated
entries.evidence: These kits can be invaluable in preventing sensory meltdowns or shutdowns, and they can also provide comfort to individuals on the spectrum.
entries.notes: Source is an undated Town of BWG notice on BradfordToday. Kits can be reserved in the library catalogue or by phone and must be returned to the service desk, not the drop box.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (Capitol Theatre, Port Hope)
entries.description: Port Hope's professional theatre runs relaxed performances for disabled and neurodiverse audiences: house lights stay on at 30%, loud noises are softened, fewer seats are sold so people can get up and move, there is a quiet space upstairs, and a venue guide and fact sheets explain the visit in advance. Staff and volunteers are trained for these shows.
entries.cost_note: Adult tickets $25; one free ticket for a support person
entries.evidence: The house lights above the audience will be left on a low level, loud noises may be softer, and there will be more empty seats available so you can get up and move around when you need to.
entries.notes: 2026 season had four relaxed performances (May 24, June 21, July 19 and August 30); check for the 2027 season.

entries.name: Canadian War Museum
entries.description: The Canadian War Museum in Ottawa warns visitors that its exhibitions are immersive and multi-sensory, with sound effects in several areas and lower lighting, and lends ear defenders (reserve ahead or ask at Information); visitors are welcome to wear noise-cancelling headphones, and there are no strobe or flashing lights in the ongoing exhibitions.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission
entries.evidence: Visitors are welcome to wear noise-cancelling headphones during their visit. Ear defenders are also available for reservation (click here) or upon arrival at Information.
entries.notes: Supports are general sensory accommodations rather than a dedicated autism program.

entries.name: Sensory Friendly D&D (Vaughan Public Libraries)
entries.description: A library program in Vaughan where adults and teens, with a caregiver or support worker if they wish, play Dungeons & Dragons in a more accessible, sensory-friendly session and connect with others in the community.
entries.cost_note: Registration required; cost not stated
entries.evidence: For adults and teens and a caregiver or support worker, this program is intended to be a more accessible D&D experience.
entries.notes: Sessions listed at Carrville Library on Tuesdays 6:00 to 8:00 PM (October 20 and November 3, 2026 when checked). Age ranges reflect 'adults and teens'.

entries.name: Sensory-friendly Skate and Sensory-Friendly Swim (City of Guelph)
entries.description: Guelph runs a drop-in Sensory-friendly Skate (dimmed lighting, no music, a smaller group of skaters, no buzzers or whistles; skate aids, wheelchairs and sledges welcome) and a Sensory-Friendly Swim for children, youth and adults with autism, sensory processing or learning disabilities, designed to reduce stimuli in the pool.
entries.cost_note: Drop-in fee not stated; accompanying adults or support persons skate free
entries.evidence: Dimmed lighting, no music, a smaller group of skaters, no buzzers or whistles.
entries.notes: Skating season runs September 2026 to May 2027 at Victoria Road Recreation Centre and West End Community Centre; accompanying adults or support persons skate free. Pre-register for drop-ins online, in person or by phone up to 23 hours before. The swim page does not give times on the text we could read.

entries.name: Games Café for Autistic & Neurodivergent Adults (Oshawa Public Libraries)
entries.description: A weekly social meetup at Oshawa Public Libraries' McLaughlin Branch where independent autistic and neurodivergent adults (18+) play games and get to know each other.
entries.cost_note: Not stated
entries.evidence: A weekly social meetup for independent neurodivergent adults 18+.
entries.notes: Listed on the library's home page as a weekly series (next session Oct 21, 4:00 to 6:00 pm, McLaughlin Branch, when checked); the event pages need JavaScript, so details beyond the title and one-line description could not be read. A 'Sensory Zone' event is also listed.

entries.name: Sensory Swim (Town of Aurora)
entries.description: Aurora's Sensory Swim at the Aurora Family Leisure Complex pool is for swimmers of all ages and abilities who have sensory sensitivity, including autistic people, with no background music or announcements and fewer swimmers in the pool. The town's page also suggests items like ear bands, goggles and nose clips that can help.
entries.cost_note: Drop-in fee not stated in the Sensory Swim section
entries.evidence: During this time, there will be no background auditory music or announcements, and reduced number of swimmers per swim.
entries.notes: Fall 2026 schedule (October 4 to December 6, 2026): Sundays 1:30 to 2:30 pm at the A.F.L.C. Pool; page updated July 17, 2026. This page was also fetched by another topic's agent (swimming), so check for a duplicate entry there.

entries.name: Snoezelen Nook sensory room and adapted swims (City of Hamilton)
entries.description: The City of Hamilton books one-hour sessions in the Snoezelen Nook, a sensory room at Westmount Recreation Centre with equipment for relaxation through light, touch and sound, and runs adapted drop-in swims and SwimAbilities lessons scheduled when no other lessons are in the pool, to reduce sensory distractions and change-room waits.
entries.cost_note: Snoezelen Nook $4.60 per participant; support persons free in adapted programs
entries.evidence: A one hour program time designed for anyone living with disabilities or additional support needs to access a fun, multi-sensory environment with specialized equipment that promotes relaxation and stimulation through light, touch, and sound.
entries.notes: These are adapted programs for people with disabilities or additional needs, held at city recreation centres. SwimAbilities is for ages 3 to 18 with a support person in the water. This page was also fetched by another topic's agent, so check for a duplicate entry.

entries.name: Light Up the Creek (Downtown Stoney Creek)
entries.description: Three free autism sensory-friendly Friday evenings in Downtown Stoney Creek (Hamilton) on December 4, 11 and 18, 2026, from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m., with sensory-friendly lighting, family activities through the village, visits with Santa and a tree lighting on opening night.
entries.cost_note: Admission is free
entries.evidence: Light Up the Creek brings three free, autism sensory-friendly Friday evenings to Downtown Stoney Creek on December 4, 11 and 18, 2026, from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m.
entries.notes: A seasonal event series, not a year-round place: presented by the Canadian National Autism Foundation and the Downtown Stoney Creek BIA along King Street East (Lake Ave to New Mountain). Listings found on HamiltonEvents.ca and Active Parents; no organiser page was fetched. Consider dropping if the team does not want CNAF-run events.

entries.name: Sensory Kits (Caledon Public Library)
entries.description: Caledon Public Library lends sensory support kits for use in the library, with self-soothing tactile items meant to comfort autistic and neurodiverse people and reduce anxiety and stress in unfamiliar places.
entries.cost_note: Borrowed for in-library use; cost not stated
entries.evidence: Sensory support kits are designed to provide comfort to autistic and neuro-diverse people through self-soothing tactile items that can help reduce anxiety and stress in unfamiliar environments.
entries.notes: Listed in the library's Library of Things; the page does not say which branches hold kits or what is inside. Caledon has several branch listings; left unmatched.

entries.name: Relaxed Performances (Magnus Theatre)
entries.description: Magnus Theatre in Thunder Bay stages relaxed performances for people with intellectual or learning disabilities, sensory processing conditions, dementia or autism: noise and movement in the audience are fine, light, sound and startling effects are toned down, and a low-sensory area is open if the show becomes overwhelming. Tickets are pay what you want.
entries.cost_note: Pay What You Want tickets for relaxed performances; PAL cards accepted
entries.address: 10 Algoma St. S, Thunder Bay, ON P7B 3A7
entries.evidence: A low-sensory area will be accessible if the performance becomes overwhelming.
entries.notes: The 'next relaxed performance dates' on the page are Elf! The Musical matinees on Wednesday December 4th and Sunday December 8th, which match December 2024, so the page may not have been updated; confirm 2026-27 relaxed performances with the box office.

entries.name: Sensory-Friendly Screenings (Cineplex)
entries.description: Cineplex theatres across Canada show newly released films for autistic people and their families with the lights up and the sound down. Screenings are on Saturday mornings every 4 to 6 weeks, and every ticket is priced at the child admission rate.
entries.cost_note: All tickets at the child admission rate, on sale the Tuesday before
entries.evidence: This program provides a sensory-friendly environment for individuals with autism spectrum disorders and their families to view newly released films in a lights up, sound down environment in theatres across the country.
entries.notes: The page does not list which theatres take part; families check showtimes at their local Cineplex. Also described on Cineplex's accessibility page.

entries.name: Sensory-friendly hours (Walmart Canada)
entries.description: Walmart's 403 Canadian stores keep sensory-friendly hours from opening until 10 a.m. every Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, with no music or radio ads, no announcements or paging except emergencies, and only still, low-sensory images on the TV walls.
entries.cost_note: Regular store prices; no extra cost for the quieter hours
entries.evidence: All the retailer’s stores coast-to-coast will take steps to reduce visual and auditory stimuli from store opening until 10 a.m. local time every Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.
entries.notes: Newest sources found are from July 2024 (Canadian Grocer, OrilliaMatters), slightly over two years old; nothing found saying it ended, but confirm with Walmart Canada. Walmart consulted Sensory Friendly Solutions; a spokesperson told OrilliaMatters stores could not dim their lights.

entries.name: Canadian Museum of History
entries.description: The Canadian Museum of History in Gatineau, Quebec, explains its immersive, multi-sensory exhibitions in advance (sound effects, lower lighting, which halls are brightest and which are quieter), welcomes noise-cancelling headphones, and lends ear defenders free at Information or by reservation.
entries.cost_note: Museum admission; ear defenders free
entries.evidence: Visitors are welcome to wear noise-cancelling headphones during their visit. Ear defenders are also available for reservation (click here) or upon arrival at Information.
entries.notes: Quieter spaces named: the Canadian Stamp Collection and First Peoples Hall. Same sensory information style as its sister museum, the Canadian War Museum (Ottawa).

unverified.name: Sensory-Friendly Skates (City of Pembroke Parks & Recreation)
unverified.reason: A 2025-26 pilot of four skates (no music, reduced capacity, 1:1 support on ice) that ended March 2026 'to assess the feasibility' of a permanent program; no 2026-27 dates found.

unverified.name: Autism Comfort package (Chelsea Hotel, Toronto)
unverified.reason: An older travel-trade article describes an Autism Comfort package with social scripts and fidget kits, but the hotel's current accessibility page does not mention it, and the article page would not load (TLS error).

unverified.name: Sensory-friendly shopping hours (Sobeys, Safeway, IGA, Foodland, FreshCo)
unverified.reason: Newest source found is from December 2019 (store-by-store schedules); Sobeys' own pages returned HTTP 403, so it could not be confirmed that the program still runs.

unverified.name: Sensory-friendly day (Flying Squirrel trampoline parks: Hamilton, Ottawa, London, Whitby)
unverified.reason: Destination Ontario and Active Parents say the first Tuesday of each month is sensory-friendly, but the Hamilton park's own Special Hours page does not mention it; not confirmable on its own site.

unverified.name: We Rock the Spectrum Kid's Gym (Oakville)
unverified.reason: Listed by Destination Ontario (245 Wyecroft Road), but its own website could not be found (guessed domain does not resolve); not confirmed open.

unverified.name: Sensory Friendly Sunday Mornings (Fort Henry, Kingston)
unverified.reason: Only an archived 2019 page describes it; the event page now returns 404 and Fort Henry's site shows no sensory program.

unverified.name: Sensory-friendly skates (Atlas Tube Recreation Centre, Lakeshore)
unverified.reason: Only source is a March 2023 news story (dimmed lights, reduced noise); no current schedule found.

unverified.name: Sensory Friendly Saturdays (Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery)
unverified.reason: Paused; the gallery says a redesigned 'Access Saturday' returns by January 2027. The gallery itself is kept as an entry for its everyday sensory supports.

unverified.name: Niagara Falls Convention Centre (KultureCity Sensory Inclusive certification)
unverified.reason: Only source is a January 4, 2023 trade article (sensory bags, quiet spaces, trained staff); the centre's own site could not be found (guessed domains do not resolve), so current certification is unconfirmed.

unverified.name: Sensory-friendly Santa (Bayshore Shopping Centre, Ottawa)
unverified.reason: Event page returned no readable text; the mall's site has no sensory information; seasonal and unconfirmed for 2026.
